scenes.title: Bathroom partition mounting styles
scenes.say: Every toilet partition is held up one of four ways.
From the floor with a headrail, from the floor alone, from steel above the ceiling, or from both the floor and the ceiling.
Overhead braced is the most common style.

facts: A floor that takes anchors. No ceiling structure.
scenes.say: The pilasters are anchored to the floor, and an aluminum headrail ties their tops to the walls.
It needs no ceiling structure and installs almost anywhere.
Floor mounted partitions drop the headrail.
Each pilaster is bolted into a structural concrete floor, with nothing overhead.

facts: An open look and high ceilings
scenes.say: The room looks more open, which suits high ceilings.
Ceiling hung partitions never touch the floor.

facts: Structural steel, engineered for the load
scenes.say: They hang from structural steel above the ceiling, so the steel has to be designed to carry them.

facts: A clear floor that's easy to clean
scenes.say: The whole floor stays clear for cleaning.
Floor to ceiling partitions are anchored at both ends.

facts: A concrete floor and structure at the ceiling
scenes.say: Every pilaster goes into the concrete floor and into structure at the ceiling.
It's the most stable choice for heavy use, like schools.
No structure above the ceiling? Overhead braced or floor mounted. A floor that can't take anchors? Ceiling hung. Heavy use? Floor to ceiling.
